evidenceQualityLayer.highQualityCondition: PROVISIONAL FOUR-FACTOR PRODUCT for ordinary structural comparison (PRIMARY × PRIMARY): evidenceType × knowledgeLevel × confidence × reliabilityFlags. Role-coverage is not a factor. PROVISIONAL — PENDING C-25/X-4.
evidenceQualityLayer.multiplier: SUPERSEDED / ANNULLED — NO REPLACEMENT RANGE PENDING C-25/X-4
evidenceQualityLayer.lowQualityCondition: Below 0.4 = low-quality divergence; below 0.2 = excluded entirely. Thresholds 0.7 / 0.5 / 0.4 / 0.2 retained; not recalibrated.
evidenceQualityLayer.action: Ordinary domain PRIMARY × PRIMARY: multiplier ≥ 0.7 standard divergence weight; 0.4–0.7 flagged but reduced; < 0.4 noted, NO Contradiction record. DEC-8 domain PRIMARY × CONTEXTUAL on triggering Q1/Q5 is a separate state-③ quality-admissibility check only (≥ 0.5), OWNER-ADOPTED CORRECTION — PROVISIONAL, PENDING C-25/X-4. DEC-8 is not a structural resolver score, not AGREE/DIVERGE tally, not HIGH-resolver logic, and not priority-1 coverage.

divergenceClassification.qualityThreshold: Provisional four-factor product ≥ 0.7 on agreement-contributing PRIMARY × PRIMARY questions
divergenceClassification.resolutionPath: No analyst intervention required for this state alone; standard methodology proceeds
divergenceClassification.output: ★★★ STRONG signal pattern + 0 contradiction records (per schema sheet 11)

divergenceClassification.triggerCondition: Effective AGREE 5–6 among PRIMARY × PRIMARY comparable questions. DEC-7b: for NF/SFP vs NF/SFJ the ordinary 5–6 floor still applies; one agreeing Q11 HIGH does not replace it (sheet 7!D6 override does not apply to that pair).
divergenceClassification.highWeightCondition: At least one HIGH resolver defined for the active pair AGREES, and that resolver is PRIMARY for both respondents (DEC-3)
divergenceClassification.qualityThreshold: Provisional four-factor product ≥ 0.5 on agreement-contributing PRIMARY × PRIMARY questions
divergenceClassification.resolutionPath: Co-presence note appended for diverging axes; one or more low-severity Contradiction records may issue

divergenceClassification.triggerCondition: Exactly one senior-tier and one line_level-tier respondent. Q1 and/or Q5 materially DIVERGE with senior side PRIMARY and line-level side CONTEXTUAL. Agreement foundation: ≥ 5 non-governance PRIMARY × PRIMARY AGREE, each with provisional four-factor ≥ 0.5.
divergenceClassification.highWeightCondition: HIGH-weight pair-resolvers may agree or diverge — not determinative for this state
divergenceClassification.qualityThreshold: DEC-8 OWNER-ADOPTED CORRECTION — PROVISIONAL, PENDING C-25/X-4: on each triggering Q1/Q5 (PRIMARY × CONTEXTUAL) the provisional four-factor product must be ≥ 0.5 as a quality-admissibility check only. Not a structural resolver score; not AGREE/DIVERGE tally; not HIGH-resolver logic; not priority-1 coverage.
divergenceClassification.resolutionPath: The senior-tier respondent's signal pattern is primary; the line-level respondent's observation is recorded as the operational layer.
divergenceClassification.output: ★ WEAK signal pattern + SPLIT annotation + 1 medium-severity Contradiction record (cross_respondent_same_side)

divergenceClassification.triggerCondition: All HIGH resolvers defined for the active pair DIVERGE, each PRIMARY for both respondents, provisional quality ≥ 0.5 (e.g. {Q4-A, Q4-B} split AND {Q7-A, Q7-B} split for NT/STJ vs NT/STP). Canonical one-HIGH pair NF/SFP vs NF/SFJ is intercepted by sheet 12 priority 3a (DEC-7) and is not auto-④-A.
divergenceClassification.highWeightCondition: All defined HIGH resolvers fail (PRIMARY × PRIMARY DIVERGE)
divergenceClassification.qualityThreshold: Provisional four-factor product ≥ 0.5 on the failing HIGH questions (genuine divergence, not low-quality artifact)
divergenceClassification.resolutionPath: PRACTITIONER ESCALATION REQUIRED — within-pair distinction compromised
divergenceClassification.output: BLOCKED — no signal pattern issued + 1 high-severity Contradiction record (cross_respondent_same_side)

divergenceClassification.triggerCondition: One respondent's signals concentrate on an environment OUTSIDE the candidate pair (unordered — either respondent). INELIGIBLE and UNRESOLVED do not create pair-identification failure.
divergenceClassification.highWeightCondition: Pair identification itself fails — pair-resolver weights inapplicable
divergenceClassification.resolutionPath: Engine flags candidate ④-B (evidence outside candidate pair detected). PRACTITIONER CONFIRMATION REQUIRED before final ④-B. Adding R3 does NOT resolve ④-B.
divergenceClassification.output: BLOCKED — no signal pattern issued + 1 critical-severity Contradiction record (contradictionType = cross_respondent_same_side)

edgeCases.edgeCase: Agreement-count criteria satisfied but environment coherence ambiguous
edgeCases.trigger: Agreement-count criteria for ①/② satisfied, but agreed questions do not resolve to a coherent environment pattern
edgeCases.classification: ANALYST / PRACTITIONER REVIEW — no automatic state assigned
edgeCases.rationale: Agreement-count criteria for ①/② may be satisfied while the agreement environment coherence is ambiguous. There is NO canonical coherence rule in the corpus. The engine MUST NOT infer one and MUST NOT auto-classify this as ④-B. Route to analyst / practitioner review until an explicit canonical coherence rule is authored.

edgeCases.edgeCase: All defined HIGH resolvers agree but total PRIMARY × PRIMARY AGREE < 5
edgeCases.trigger: All HIGH resolvers defined for the active pair AGREE (PRIMARY both), but only 3–4 remaining PRIMARY × PRIMARY questions agree
edgeCases.classification: PARTIAL CONVERGENCE — but flag LOW CONFIDENCE
edgeCases.rationale: For multi-HIGH pairs: pair-resolvers are authoritative for the specific pair. Agreement on all defined HIGH resolvers overrides the 5/11 total threshold for this pair. Append: "High-weight pair confirmation with partial screening agreement". DEC-7b: this override does NOT apply to the canonical one-HIGH pair NF/SFP vs NF/SFJ. State ② for that pair still requires the ordinary 5–6 PRIMARY × PRIMARY agreements. A single agreeing Q11 HIGH does not replace the confirmation floor. Number 5–6 is unchanged.

edgeCases.trigger: Q4 and Q7 disagree on direction for NT/STJ vs NT/STP pair
edgeCases.classification: PARTIAL CONVERGENCE with LOW CONFIDENCE flag if total ≥ 5; otherwise ANALYST REVIEW — no automatic state assigned
edgeCases.rationale: Split pair-resolver result removes the ability to cleanly lock the pair. Treat as single-resolver confirmation with reduced confidence. ④-A is NOT reachable here: automatic ④-A requires divergence of all HIGH resolvers defined for the active pair (PRIMARY both). Canonical one-HIGH Q11 DIVERGE is intercepted by priority 3a (DEC-7), not ④-A.

edgeCases.edgeCase: R1 R2 same role level, systematic Q1/Q5 diverge
edgeCases.trigger: Both PARTNER_MD but disagree on Axis 1 and Axis 5
edgeCases.classification: EXCLUDED FROM ③ ROLE-LEVEL SPLIT. ANALYST REVIEW — no automatic state assigned.
edgeCases.rationale: ROLE-LEVEL SPLIT requires a genuine seniority-tier difference between the two respondents per the state ③ definition on sheet 5 of this workbook. Same-tier divergence on governance axes indicates genuine disagreement, not an observation-layer difference. Same-tier divergence on Q1/Q5 is genuine disagreement, not an observation-layer split. Q1/Q5 alone do not satisfy the quantified ④-A trigger; automatic ④-A requires BOTH HIGH-weight pair resolvers to diverge.

edgeCases.edgeCase: R2 produces third env outside candidate pair
edgeCases.trigger: One respondent's signals concentrate on an environment OUTSIDE the candidate pair (e.g. NT/STJ vs SFJ/SFP, unordered — either respondent).
edgeCases.rationale: Engine may detect and flag the out-of-pair signal. It may NOT finalise ④-B. Practitioner confirms pair-identification failure. Third respondent does NOT resolve.

edgeCases.trigger: BOTH respondents answered E to all HIGH resolvers defined for the active pair
edgeCases.rationale: Pair-resolvers cannot be evaluated. This is absence of evidence, not genuine divergence. HIGH cardinality is read per active pair from sheet 2. ④-A is reachable ONLY when all defined HIGH resolvers DIVERGE at PRIMARY × PRIMARY with quality ≥ 0.5, except the one-HIGH pair which is intercepted by DEC-7. No Contradiction record is emitted from this coverage outcome.

edgeCases.edgeCase: Mixed-E pattern correlated with role tier (v3.1 NEW)
edgeCases.trigger: line-level-tier respondent systematically answers E on Axis 1 and Axis 5; senior-tier respondent answers substantively
edgeCases.classification: ③ ROLE-LEVEL SPLIT — not coverage gap
edgeCases.rationale: Line-level × Q1 / Q5 default UseClass is CONTEXTUAL (sheet 11). Systematic line-level E on Q1/Q5 is the expected structural outcome of operational altitude, not by itself a coverage failure, and is not a seniority-as-quality penalty.

edgeCases.trigger: BOTH respondents answered F (cannot answer) to Q11
edgeCases.classification: PRECONDITION / COVERAGE OUTCOME: NF/SFP determination impossible
edgeCases.rationale: Scoped to the NF/SFP vs NF/SFJ pair and the Q11 discriminator family only. Q11 is not a resolver for the other four production pairs. NOT a divergence state. PRACTITIONER REVIEW. No automatic cross-instrument fallback. ST_Environment_Diagnostic_v2.xlsx is NOT a valid automatic fallback: its canonical scoring notes state that NF/SFP has direct-name coverage of only 3 questions and warn that an NF/SFP signal there may be an instrument artifact.

edgeCases.trigger: Both respondents have acquisition_framing_contamination flag on the same questions
edgeCases.rationale: v3.1: shared reliability flags do NOT increase confidence — they indicate both respondents are subject to the same bias. The agreement is not independent triangulation.

edgeCases.edgeCase: Quality multiplier < 0.4 across all questions (v3.1 NEW)
edgeCases.trigger: ≥ 8 of 11 questions have PRIMARY × PRIMARY comparable comparison unavailable OR provisional PRIMARY × PRIMARY four-factor score < 0.4. Number 8/11 unchanged. DEC-8 PRIMARY × CONTEXTUAL state-③ check is not counted here.
edgeCases.classification: PRECONDITION / COVERAGE OUTCOME: COVERAGE INSUFFICIENT — comparator output suppressed. This is NOT a divergence state and does NOT enter the five-state enum.
edgeCases.rationale: Updated coverage predicate (number 8/11 retained): a question counts as insufficient if PRIMARY × PRIMARY comparison is unavailable OR provisional PRIMARY × PRIMARY score < 0.4. If ≥ 8 of 11: COVERAGE INSUFFICIENT. Do NOT issue Contradiction records. DEC-8 PRIMARY × CONTEXTUAL quality-admissibility checks are excluded from this count.

accuracyChecks.check:
Run all six checks in sequence. Multiple failures may compound. Decision rules:

 • All 6 PASS → proceed to instrument selection (sheet 5)
 • Any 1-2 FAIL with corrective action available → send corrective message; re-run Layer 1; return to triage
 • Check 5 FAIL OR Check 6 FAIL → DO NOT serve 35-Q (instrument cannot fix the underlying problem); route to analyst workspace via Contradiction record (sheet 4) OR practitioner escalation
 • Any 3+ checks FAIL → practitioner escalation (sheet 7)
 • Client cannot provide corrective respondent → practitioner escalation (sheet 7)

contradictionTiers.tier:
When BOTH dimensions activate, the combined tier is the more severe of the two — not an average. Examples:

 • Reliability tier MODERATE + Contradiction tier FEW → effective tier MODERATE
 • Reliability tier MODERATE + Contradiction tier MANY → effective tier MANY (higher of the two)
 • Reliability tier HIGH + Contradiction tier NONE → effective tier HIGH
 • Reliability tier CRITICAL + Contradiction tier ANY → effective tier CRITICAL/BLOCKING
 • Reliability tier ANY + Contradiction tier BLOCKING → effective tier BLOCKING

Rationale: a chain is as reliable as its weakest link. Per ST_Analyst_Methodology.xlsx §6 Risk Output Composition Procedure: confidence is the MINIMUM across constituent assessments, not the average.

→ All quality gates pass + 0 contradictions: EXIT TRIAGE; route to analyst workspace for standard review.
→ Any trigger condition fires: ENTER TRIAGE (step 2 below).

decisionTree.conditionAction:
TRIAGE ENTERED. Identify which of six trigger conditions fired (sheet 1):
TRIGGER 1 weak signal · TRIGGER 2 co-presence · TRIGGER 3 partial · TRIGGER 4 negative-only · TRIGGER 5 reliability saturation (v3.1) · TRIGGER 6 contradiction blocking (v3.1)
decisionTree.exitConditions:
→ TRIGGER 6 BLOCKING: Skip to Step 7 (practitioner escalation).
→ TRIGGER 4 NEGATIVE-ONLY: Skip to Step 7.
→ TRIGGER 5 SATURATION: Skip Step 4 (do not serve 35-Q); proceed to Step 6.
→ TRIGGERS 1, 2, 3: Proceed to Step 3.

decisionTree.conditionAction: Run Accuracy Check (sheet 2). All 6 checks: Tenure · Role · Event-anchored answers · Multiple respondents · Gate pattern (v3.1) · Evidence-machinery quality (v3.1).
decisionTree.exitConditions:
→ Checks 1/2/3/4 fail with corrective respondent available: send corrective message; re-run Layer 1; return to Step 1.
→ Check 5 OR Check 6 fail: skip Step 4 (instrument cannot fix); proceed to Step 6.
→ 3+ checks fail: Step 7.
→ All pass: Step 4.

decisionTree.conditionAction: Select 35-Q instrument(s) per Sheet 5. Send client message. Await responses from 8-15 respondents.
decisionTree.exitConditions:
→ Responses received: Step 5.

decisionTree.exitConditions:
→ CONFIRMED: Step 6 with confirmed candidate signal pattern.
→ PARTIAL (one CONFIRMED, other PARTIAL): Step 6 with CONFIRMED pattern.
→ MIXED: Step 6 with co-present signal pattern.
→ NOT_[ENV] in co-presence pair: serve OTHER 35-Q (return to Step 4).
→ All NOT_[ENV] / both PARTIAL / MIXED with new third env: Step 7.

→ Combined tier ≤ MODERATE: route to standard analyst review queue per ST_Analyst_Methodology.xlsx §4.
→ Combined tier MANY: priority analyst review, senior analyst preferred.
→ Combined tier HIGH/CRITICAL/BLOCKING: Step 7.

decisionTree.step: WHAT THIS DECISION TREE DOES NOT DO

This decision tree does NOT lock environment codes. It does NOT exit to "environment code resolved" or "environment code locked." Its terminal states are either: (a) routing to analyst workspace with a signal pattern + reliability/contradiction tier annotations; or (b) routing to practitioner. The analyst or practitioner makes the final call. Per ST_Analyst_Methodology.xlsx §1: no Layer 1 instrument names a final environment as the deliverable.
